note: Fillable stub for educator-written prerequisite rationales and named misconceptions on the frozen starter set (29 fnd- skills). Software must not invent these claims — leave edgeRationales and misconceptions empty until a human educator writes them. The two records in examples[] are FORMAT ILLUSTRATIONS only (example: true, example-* ids); they must never be imported as real graph content. Workbench: educator-edge-audit.html. Fold a completed export with npm run graph:import, then npm run graph:edges && npm run graph:misconceptions.

edgeRationale.rationale: why an educator asserts that `to` cannot be learned before `from` is at least secure

misconception.id: mis-<skillId> (optional; assigned on fold if omitted)
misconception.description: the named wrong reading a learner holds
misconception.signal: what the learner does when they hold that reading (observable on an item)

examples.rationale: EXAMPLE ONLY — not a pedagogical claim about a real skill. Format: one or two sentences an educator would defend, stating why A must be secure before teaching B.

examples.description: EXAMPLE ONLY — the wrong reading a learner holds (a named model, not a vague 'confused').
examples.signal: EXAMPLE ONLY — what the learner does when they hold that reading (something an item can observe).
